Baselined 2026-07-26. RE-BASELINED the same day, upward, after the gate found a flaw in
itself: it had been matching an order and a directive anywhere in the same FILE, and its
own new test file - which names six orders - cross-matched immediately. Whole-file
matching counted 57 directives bound; requiring the directive to sit within two lines of

its order counts 36 - and exposed that six section labels named the order loosely ('COUNTY 10 D1') rather than by a key the gate resolves, which relabelling fixed, taking the bound count to 55. The larger number was wrong and this file was too short. A gate that
measures debt is the last place an over-count is tolerable.
So: 102 binding directives, 55 bound, 47 recorded here. The number may only go down.
Three of the classes below are bindable work that has not been done. One is not: a
Principal gate on a live cutover cannot be decided by CI, and a test claiming otherwise
would be precisely the false claim this gate exists to catch.

AUDIT-DEPTH-001:D8.reason: Not code-testable and correctly so: it is a PRINCIPAL GATE on a live cutover or an external credential. Nothing in this repository can decide whether the Principal has given the go, and a test that claimed to would be the false claim this gate exists to stop. Enforced by the deploy record, not by CI.

ORG-WORKSPACE-TENANCY-001:D7.reason: NOT a labelling gap - HALF THIS DIRECTIVE IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, and that was found by trying to bind it. D7 has two halves. The first, seeding the founding superadmin into a default org plus workspace, IS built and cites the directive at boltrig/api/initiate.py:104. The second, 'force a password rotation before prod exposure so a weak seed admin is never the live prod gate', is NOT: there is no must_change_password on User, no rotation flag, and nothing in the login path that compels a change. What exists instead is a different control - initiate calls validate_password_strength, so a weak seed password is refused at seeding time, and `boltrig set-password` allows a MANUAL rotation. That addresses the same hazard by another route, which is why this is recorded as an open divergence rather than a silent one, with a shorter expiry than the rest. Deciding whether the strength check satisfies D7 or whether forced rotation must be built is a matter for the court, not for whoever next edits this file.

ORG-WORKSPACE-TENANCY-001:D9.reason: A DELIVERY-PROCESS directive, not a property of the running system: 'copy only the opbox auth/tenancy core, never its domain models, and deliver in phases, reconciling with COUNTY 7'. Two of its three clauses are about how the work was sequenced and are spent - the phases happened and the reconciliation with COUNTY 7 is what the first-party auth tests now prove. The durable clause is 'never its domain models', which an architecture check could bind by asserting no opbox domain model reaches this tree. That check is not written, and inventing a keyword list for it without reading the opbox model surface would produce a test that passes for the wrong reason.
